title.narrative: Contribution to the Basket Fund of the MAPP/OAS in Colombia

description.narrative: The MAPP/OAS in Colombia seeks to support the government and its citizens in achieving comprehensive and sustainable peace with all armed groups across the national territory. As a strategic partner, the Mission offers an innovative and adaptable model of international cooperation, built on over two decades of experience, territorial presence, and continuous engagement with stakeholders. This enables it to provide timely and context-sensitive recommendations to the Colombian State, addressing both achievements and ongoing challenges in peace consolidation. The 2025–2027 Institutional Strategic Plan is based on process and results-oriented management, aligning three strategic objectives with twelve mission and support processes. Following a detailed analysis of strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats, MAPP/OAS reaffirmed the relevance of its flexible mandate, especially in regions most affected by conflict. In 2025/26, the Mission will play a key role in peace dialogues, strengthen institutions through knowledge sharing, and promote environmental governance and community participation. Its priorities include consolidating its support model, positioning its expertise for policy advocacy, contributing to environmental protection in conflict zones, and advancing gender and women’s rights agendas. Capacity building for dialogue and conflict transformation remains central, particularly for actors in socio-environmental conflicts and peace processes. The Mission will continue to provide analysis and recommendations on security, community impacts, and environmental issues, including the use of anti-personnel mines and contamination of water sources. Each year, MAPP/OAS adjusts its focus based on contextual analysis. In 2025, it will prioritise peace dialogues, victims’ rights, environmental and civilian impacts, safety conditions, implementation of the Final Peace Agreement, community engagement, transitional justice, and capacity building for peace.
